words.enDefinition: A method that estimates regression coefficients by minimizing the sum of squared residuals.

examples.en: The class used ordinary least squares to estimate the association between schooling and hourly pay.
examples.zh: 全班使用「普通最小二乘法」估计受教育程度与小时工资之间的关联。

examples.en: In the worksheet, ordinary least squares selects the line with the smallest squared residual sum.
examples.zh: 练习纸上的「普通最小二乘法」选出残差平方和最小的一条直线。

words.enDefinition: A parameter attached to an explanatory term that determines how that term enters the fitted outcome.

examples.en: The regression coefficient gives the fitted pay change for one more year of schooling at fixed experience.
examples.zh: 在工作经验不变时，「回归系数」给出受教育年限每增加一年对应的工资拟合变化。

examples.en: We checked the units of the regression coefficient before describing its size in the report.
examples.zh: 我们先核对「回归系数」的单位，再在报告里解释系数大小。

words.enDefinition: The change in the model outcome associated with a change in one variable while other variables remain fixed.

examples.en: The partial effect of schooling in the example is evaluated at a fixed level of experience.
examples.zh: 示例中，在工作经验水平不变时评估受教育程度的「偏效应」。

examples.en: In the nonlinear model, the partial effect varies with the initial level of the explanatory variable.
examples.zh: 在非线性模型中，「偏效应」随解释变量的初始水平而变化。

words.enDefinition: The average of model-based partial effects over the relevant observations or population.

examples.en: We computed the average partial effect across workers with different levels of experience in the exercise.
examples.zh: 练习中，我们对经验水平不同的劳动者计算「平均偏效应」。

examples.en: The average partial effect summarizes the fitted changes that differ across individuals in our example.
examples.zh: 「平均偏效应」概括示例中不同个体各自的拟合变动。

words.enDefinition: A regression model with more than one explanatory variable for the same outcome.

examples.en: The multiple regression model includes prior grades and attendance when relating study hours to test scores.
examples.zh: 「多元回归模型」分析学习时数与测试成绩的关系时，同时纳入先前成绩和出勤率。

examples.en: We compared a multiple regression model with one that included only attendance in the classroom example.
examples.zh: 在课堂示例中，我们比较了「多元回归模型」和只纳入出勤率的模型。

words.enDefinition: the constant in a regression equation, giving the fitted value when the nonconstant model terms equal zero

examples.en: The regression intercept gives predicted wages when every regressor is zero in the simplified example.
examples.zh: 在简化示例中，各解释变量都为零时，「回归截距」给出预测工资。

examples.en: We discussed whether the regression intercept had a meaningful interpretation given the range of schooling.
examples.zh: 考虑到受教育年限的取值范围，我们讨论了「回归截距」是否具有实际含义。

words.enDefinition: the proportional change in one variable per unit change in another, represented locally by a log-level slope

examples.en: The semi-elasticity links one more year of schooling to an approximate percentage change in fitted wages.
examples.zh: 「半弹性」把受教育年限多一年与拟合工资的近似百分比变化联系起来。

examples.en: We used the semi-elasticity to interpret the schooling term in a model with log wages.
examples.zh: 我们用「半弹性」解读对数工资模型里的受教育程度项。

words.enDefinition: A variable whose inclusion in an analysis distorts the intended causal comparison.

examples.en: Attendance after assignment can be a bad control when the target is the total effect of tutoring.
examples.zh: 要估计辅导的总效应时，分配后的出勤情况可能是「不当控制变量」。

examples.en: The tutor explained why a bad control can change the target of the classroom estimate.
examples.zh: 老师解释为什么「不当控制变量」会改变课堂估计所针对的效应。

words.enDefinition: To interpret or evaluate a model change without changing the values of the other variables.

examples.en: We hold other variables constant when interpreting the fitted wage change associated with one more year of schooling.
examples.zh: 我们解释受教育年限多一年所对应的工资拟合变化时，「保持其他变量不变」。

examples.en: The worksheet asks us to hold other variables constant while changing the value of attendance.
examples.zh: 练习要求我们改变出勤率的取值时，「保持其他变量不变」。

collocations: hold other variables constant in a comparison
hold other variables constant by construction
interpret a coefficient holding other variables constant

words.enDefinition: An explanatory variable with two possible values, commonly coded as zero and one.

examples.en: A binary regressor records whether each fictional student was offered a place in the programme.
examples.zh: 「二元解释变量」记录每名虚构学生是否获得项目名额。

examples.en: We set the binary regressor to one for schools that joined the programme that year.
examples.zh: 我们为当年加入项目的学校把「二元解释变量」设为一。

words.enDefinition: The category left out of a regression indicator set so other category differences are measured relative to it.

examples.en: The table names the omitted reference category below the estimates for the three training groups.
examples.zh: 表格在三个培训组的估计值下方注明「省略的参照类别」。

examples.en: Changing the omitted reference category changes which group each displayed coefficient is compared against.
examples.zh: 更换「省略的参照类别」会改变表中各系数所对应的比较基准组。

words.enDefinition: Perfect collinearity caused by including every indicator for a categorical variable together with an intercept.

examples.en: The dummy variable trap appears when the worksheet includes every school category and an intercept.
examples.zh: 练习把所有学校类别的指示变量和截距一并纳入时，出现了「虚拟变量陷阱」。

examples.en: We avoided the dummy variable trap by leaving one category out of the regression.
examples.zh: 我们在回归中省略一个类别，以避免「虚拟变量陷阱」。

words.enDefinition: A model term formed from variables together to allow the relationship for one to differ with another.

examples.en: The interaction term allows the association with training to differ between workers with different experience levels.
examples.zh: 「交互项」允许培训的相关关系随劳动者的经验水平而不同。

examples.en: We added an interaction term so the fitted tutoring relationship could differ across the two school groups.
examples.zh: 我们加入一个「交互项」，允许两组学校的辅导关联有所不同。

words.enDefinition: The mathematical form that specifies how the outcome is related to its regressors.

examples.en: The functional form allows the fitted wage increase to become smaller at higher experience levels.
examples.zh: 这种「函数形式」允许经验水平较高时，工资拟合增量变小。

examples.en: We compared two choices of functional form using the same education data in class.
examples.zh: 我们用相同的教育数据比较了两种「函数形式」的选择。

words.enDefinition: A model specification in which the outcome is logged and the regressor of interest stays in levels.

examples.en: The log-level specification uses the log of hourly wages and records schooling in years.
examples.zh: 「对数—水平设定」使用小时工资的对数，受教育程度用年数表示。

examples.en: We interpreted the log-level specification by comparing wages for workers one year apart in schooling.
examples.zh: 我们比较受教育年限相差一年的劳动者工资，以解释「对数—水平设定」。

words.enDefinition: A model specification in which the outcome stays in levels and the regressor of interest is logged.

examples.en: The level-log specification records test scores in points and takes the logarithm of study hours.
examples.zh: 「水平—对数设定」用分数表示测试成绩，并对学习时数取对数。

examples.en: The tutor asked how to interpret a ten percent change in hours under the level-log specification.
examples.zh: 老师问，在「水平—对数设定」下应如何解释学习时数变动百分之十。

words.enDefinition: A model specification in which both the outcome and the regressor of interest are logged.

examples.en: The log-log specification uses logarithms for both wages and accumulated study hours in the worksheet.
examples.zh: 练习的「双对数设定」对工资和累计学习时数都取对数。

examples.en: In this log-log specification, the slope measures the fitted elasticity of one variable with respect to another.
examples.zh: 在这个「双对数设定」中，斜率衡量一个变量相对另一个变量的拟合弹性。

words.enDefinition: A squared regressor included to let the fitted slope vary with the regressor's value.

examples.en: The quadratic term lets the fitted relationship between experience and wages bend in our classroom graph.
examples.zh: 「二次项」使课堂图里的经验与工资拟合关系可以呈现曲线。

examples.en: We kept the linear part when adding a quadratic term for experience to the model.
examples.zh: 我们往模型中加入经验的「二次项」时，保留了一次项。

words.enDefinition: a linear regression for a binary outcome, with fitted values estimating probabilities that can fall outside zero to one

examples.en: The linear probability model describes how the fitted chance of completing the course changes with attendance.
examples.zh: 「线性概率模型」描述课程完成的拟合概率如何随出勤变化。

examples.en: We noticed that the linear probability model gave one fitted value above one in the exercise.
examples.zh: 我们注意到练习中的「线性概率模型」有一个拟合值大于一。

words.enDefinition: The declared choice of variables, functional relationships, and assumptions used in an econometric model.

examples.en: We described the model specification before reporting the estimated relationship between schooling and pay in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们先说明「模型设定」，再报告受教育程度与工资的估计关系。

examples.en: The second model specification includes a term for prior experience that the first version leaves out.
examples.zh: 第二种「模型设定」纳入了第一版省略的既往经验项。

words.enDefinition: A mismatch between the chosen model and the relationship or data-generating process it is meant to represent.

examples.en: The specification error arises because the classroom model assumes a straight relationship for data generated from a curve.
examples.zh: 课堂模型假定关系是直线，但生成数据的关系是曲线，因此产生了「模型设定错误」。

examples.en: We discussed whether excluding the needed interaction represented a specification error in the wage exercise.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了在工资练习里，省略必要的交互项是否属于「模型设定错误」。

words.enDefinition: The unobserved part of the population outcome left after accounting for the regressors in the model.

examples.en: The regression disturbance in our example includes unmeasured factors that may affect an individual's wages.
examples.zh: 示例中的「回归扰动项」包含可能影响个人工资的未测量因素。

examples.en: We distinguished the regression disturbance from the numerical error computed after fitting the sample model.
examples.zh: 我们区分了「回归扰动项」和拟合样本模型后计算出的数值误差。

words.enDefinition: The assumption that the error term has mean zero at every combination of the included regressors.

examples.en: Zero conditional mean would fail if unmeasured ability systematically differed across schooling levels in our example.
examples.zh: 如果示例中不可观测的能力随受教育年限系统性变化，「零条件均值」就不成立。

examples.en: The tutor stated zero conditional mean before explaining the properties of the estimated coefficients.
examples.zh: 老师先说明「零条件均值」，再解释估计系数的性质。

words.enDefinition: An exact linear relationship among regressors that prevents their separate coefficients from being uniquely determined.

examples.en: Perfect multicollinearity arises because the worksheet includes both a full set of group indicators and an intercept.
examples.zh: 练习同时包含整套组别指示变量和截距，因此出现「完全多重共线性」。

examples.en: The tutor showed why perfect multicollinearity prevents separate estimates for two redundant explanatory variables.
examples.zh: 老师说明了为什么「完全多重共线性」会导致两个信息重复的解释变量无法分别估计系数。

words.enDefinition: A diagnostic that measures how the correlation of a regressor with other regressors inflates its coefficient's variance.

examples.en: We computed a variance inflation factor for each regressor after noticing that the two schooling measures overlap.
examples.zh: 注意到两个教育指标有重叠后，我们为每个解释变量计算「方差膨胀因子」。

examples.en: The high variance inflation factor indicates that these regressors provide limited distinct variation in our example.
examples.zh: 较高的「方差膨胀因子」表明示例中的这些解释变量能提供的独立变动有限。

words.enDefinition: Bias that occurs when an omitted cause of the outcome is associated with an included regressor.

examples.en: Omitted variable bias can arise when prior skills affect wages and are associated with schooling.
examples.zh: 先前技能影响工资且与受教育程度有关时，可能产生「遗漏变量偏误」。

examples.en: The workshop asks how omitted variable bias could change the estimated association between training and pay.
examples.zh: 工作坊要求解释「遗漏变量偏误」可能怎样改变培训与工资的估计关系。

words.enDefinition: Variation in the conditional variance of the regression disturbance across values of the regressors.

examples.en: The fan shape in the residual plot suggests possible heteroskedasticity in our classroom wage model.
examples.zh: 残差图呈扇形，提示课堂工资模型可能存在「异方差」。

examples.en: We discussed heteroskedasticity because the spread of wages rises at higher levels of experience in the exercise.
examples.zh: 练习中，经验较高时工资的离散程度更大，因此我们讨论了「异方差」。

words.enDefinition: A constant conditional variance of the regression disturbance across values of the regressors.

examples.en: The first classroom simulation assumes homoskedasticity by using the same error variance at every schooling level.
examples.zh: 第一次课堂模拟采用「同方差」假设，在各受教育水平上使用相同的误差方差。

examples.en: We compared the homoskedasticity assumption with a scenario where errors spread out as wages increase.
examples.zh: 我们把「同方差」假设与工资越高、误差越分散的情形作了比较。

words.enDefinition: An estimate of coefficient uncertainty that allows for unequal error variances under suitable sampling conditions.

examples.en: We used a heteroskedasticity-robust standard error for the coefficient in the independent classroom observations.
examples.zh: 在课堂独立观测数据中，我们为该系数使用「异方差稳健标准误」。

examples.en: The heteroskedasticity-robust standard error changed even though the wage coefficient stayed the same in the example.
examples.zh: 示例中工资系数不变，但「异方差稳健标准误」发生了变化。

words.enDefinition: An in-sample fit measure that adjusts the ordinary coefficient of determination for the number of regressors.

examples.en: Adjusted R-squared fell when the extra regressor added too little explanatory power in the worksheet.
examples.zh: 练习中，新增解释变量对解释力提升太小，「调整决定系数」反而下降。

examples.en: We compared adjusted R-squared for regressions using the same outcome and the same sample.
examples.zh: 我们比较使用同一结果变量和同一样本的各回归的「调整决定系数」。

words.enDefinition: A model in which specified conditions are imposed on the coefficients or available terms.

examples.en: The restricted model sets both schooling interaction coefficients to zero in the instructor's example.
examples.zh: 在老师的示例中，「受约束模型」将两个教育交互项的系数都设为零。

examples.en: We fitted the restricted model before comparing it with one that allows those coefficients to vary.
examples.zh: 我们先拟合「受约束模型」，再把它与允许相应系数变化的模型比较。

collocations: compare a restricted model with its unrestricted counterpart

words.enDefinition: A condition placed on one or more regression coefficients when specifying or testing a model.

examples.en: The coefficient restriction requires the two groups to have the same fitted slope in the example.
examples.zh: 示例中的「系数约束」要求两组具有相同的拟合斜率。

examples.en: We wrote the coefficient restriction before fitting the model with the shared slope in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们先写出「系数约束」，再拟合斜率共用的模型。

words.enDefinition: A least-squares method that gives different observations different weights in the sum of squared residuals.

examples.en: The worksheet uses weighted least squares to give less weight to observations with larger error variances.
examples.zh: 练习用「加权最小二乘法」降低误差方差较大观测值的权重。

examples.en: We compared weighted least squares with an estimation that gives each classroom observation equal weight.
examples.zh: 我们将「加权最小二乘法」与对每个课堂观测值给出相同权重的估计作了比较。

words.enDefinition: A value giving an observation its intended contribution to an estimate, often accounting for unequal selection or response.

examples.en: The sample weight for each fictional worker reflects the survey design used in our exercise.
examples.zh: 每名虚构劳动者的「样本权重」反映了练习中的调查抽样设计。

examples.en: We applied a sample weight before estimating the mean wage from the classroom survey records.
examples.zh: 我们先应用「样本权重」，再根据课堂调查记录估计平均工资。

words.enDefinition: The process of determining a causal effect from observed data under specified assumptions.

examples.en: The lesson on causal identification asks what evidence could distinguish training effects from selection differences.
examples.zh: 这节「因果识别」课要求找出能区分培训效应与选择差异的证据。

examples.en: We explained causal identification before interpreting the coefficient on the simulated training offer in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们先解释「因果识别」，再解读模拟培训邀请的系数。

words.enDefinition: A condition that lets researchers recover the effect of interest from the available comparisons or data.

examples.en: The identifying assumption says the two schools would otherwise have followed the same average trend.
examples.zh: 这项「识别假设」认为，在没有项目的情况下，两所学校的平均趋势相同。

examples.en: We wrote down the identifying assumption before explaining what the estimated difference might represent.
examples.zh: 我们先写明「识别假设」，再解释估计差异可能代表什么。

words.enDefinition: The outcome a unit would have under a specified treatment condition, whether observed or unobserved.

examples.en: The potential outcome under training is observed for the fictional worker who actually received it.
examples.zh: 在虚构案例中，实际参加培训的劳动者在接受培训条件下的「潜在结果」可以观测。

examples.en: Our worksheet describes a potential outcome for each of the two possible treatment conditions.
examples.zh: 练习纸分别描述了两种可能处理条件下的「潜在结果」。

words.enDefinition: The outcome a unit would have experienced under a condition different from the one actually observed.

examples.en: The counterfactual outcome is the score a tutored student would have achieved without the support.
examples.zh: 「反事实结果」是接受辅导的学生如果没有得到辅导本会取得的分数。

examples.en: We explained why the counterfactual outcome cannot be observed directly for the same student.
examples.zh: 我们解释了为什么无法直接观测同一学生的「反事实结果」。

words.enDefinition: The difference between a unit's potential outcomes under two treatment conditions.

examples.en: The individual treatment effect in the simulation compares two possible scores for the same student.
examples.zh: 在模拟中，「个体处理效应」比较同一名学生的两个可能分数。

examples.en: Only one potential outcome is observed, so the student's individual treatment effect remains unknown in practice.
examples.zh: 实际只能观测一个潜在结果，因此该学生的「个体处理效应」仍然未知。

words.enDefinition: The mean difference between potential outcomes under two treatment conditions for a specified population.

examples.en: The average treatment effect summarizes what the simulated training changes across the entire target group.
examples.zh: 「平均处理效应」概括模拟培训对整个目标人群带来的平均变化。

examples.en: We estimated the average treatment effect for the population represented by our classroom experiment.
examples.zh: 我们针对课堂实验所代表的人群估计「平均处理效应」。

words.expression: average treatment effect on the treated
words.lemma: average treatment effect on the treated
words.zhGloss: 受处理者平均处理效应
words.enDefinition: The average causal effect for the units that actually receive treatment.
acceptedZhAnswers: 受处理者平均处理效应
acceptedEnVariants: average treatment effect on the treated

examples.en: We defined the average treatment effect on the treated for the workers who received training.
examples.zh: 我们针对实际接受培训的劳动者定义「受处理者平均处理效应」。

examples.en: The tutor compared the average treatment effect on the treated with the full population average.
examples.zh: 老师比较了「受处理者平均处理效应」与全体人群的平均值。

collocations: estimate the average treatment effect on the treated
interpret the average treatment effect on the treated
average treatment effect on the treated in a subgroup

words.enDefinition: Variation in causal effects across people, groups, places, or times.

examples.en: The class explored treatment effect heterogeneity by comparing simulated course effects across two age groups.
examples.zh: 全班比较模拟课程在两个年龄组的效果，以考察「处理效应异质性」。

examples.en: Treatment effect heterogeneity matters when the average hides different responses across the schools in the example.
examples.zh: 在示例中，平均值掩盖各学校的不同反应时，「处理效应异质性」就很重要。

words.enDefinition: The process by which units receive, seek, or choose a treatment, potentially creating systematic group differences.

examples.en: Selection into treatment occurs when the more motivated fictional students are likelier to enrol in tutoring.
examples.zh: 虚构学生中，积极性较高者更可能报名辅导，这体现了「进入处理组的选择」。

examples.en: We described selection into treatment before comparing the groups' scores in the classroom case.
examples.zh: 在课堂案例中，我们先说明「进入处理组的选择」，再比较各组得分。

words.enDefinition: An unmeasured factor that influences both treatment exposure and the outcome, threatening a causal comparison.

examples.en: The instructor used motivation as a possible unobserved confounder in the example of voluntary tutoring.
examples.zh: 老师在自愿参加辅导的示例中，用积极性举例说明可能的「未观测混杂因素」。

examples.en: We asked whether an unobserved confounder could explain the gap between the two training groups.
examples.zh: 我们问「未观测混杂因素」是否可能解释两个培训组之间的差距。

words.enDefinition: A condition in which a regressor is related to the model's unobserved error term.

examples.en: Endogeneity is possible when prior skills affect both training decisions and wages in our classroom example.
examples.zh: 课堂示例中，既往技能同时影响培训决定和实测工资时，可能存在「内生性」。

examples.en: The worksheet asks what kind of endogeneity the proposed instrument is intended to address.
examples.zh: 练习问的是拟议工具变量旨在处理哪种「内生性」。

words.enDefinition: A regressor that is correlated with the disturbance in the equation being estimated.

examples.en: Training participation is an endogenous regressor if omitted motivation influences both participation and subsequent earnings.
examples.zh: 如果遗漏的积极性同时影响参与培训的决定和后续收入，培训参与就是「内生解释变量」。

examples.en: We labelled the endogenous regressor before writing the first equation in our classroom exercise.
examples.zh: 课堂练习中，我们先标出「内生解释变量」，再写下第一个方程。

words.enDefinition: Variation in a variable that is unrelated to the unobserved determinants relevant to the comparison.

examples.en: The simulated lottery provides exogenous variation in access to extra study sessions in our exercise.
examples.zh: 在练习中，模拟抽签为参加额外学习小组的机会提供了「外生变动」。

examples.en: We considered whether the timetable rule could generate exogenous variation for the hypothetical comparison.
examples.zh: 我们研究该时间表规则能否为假设比较产生「外生变动」。

collocations: use exogenous variation in a study

words.enDefinition: A situation in which the supposed outcome influences the variable proposed as its cause.

examples.en: Reverse causality is possible if better expected wages affect workers' decisions to seek further training.
examples.zh: 如果更高的预期工资影响劳动者是否寻求进一步培训，就可能存在「反向因果」。

examples.en: The class considered reverse causality before interpreting the observed association between grades and tutoring hours.
examples.zh: 全班先考虑「反向因果」，再解释成绩与辅导时数的观测关联。

words.enDefinition: Bias that arises when variables jointly determine each other, making a regressor correlated with the disturbance.

examples.en: The example shows simultaneity bias when firms and workers jointly determine both wages and hours.
examples.zh: 示例中，企业和劳动者共同决定工资和工时，从而出现「联立性偏误」。

examples.en: We distinguished simultaneity bias from a case in which an important background variable was simply omitted.
examples.zh: 我们把「联立性偏误」与单纯遗漏一个重要背景变量的情况区分开。

words.enDefinition: A study using a naturally occurring rule or event that creates a comparison resembling an experiment.

examples.en: The lesson treats the simulated eligibility change as a natural experiment under a stated assignment assumption.
examples.zh: 课程在给定分配假设下，把模拟的资格变动当作「自然实验」。

examples.en: We discussed whether the change in classroom schedules could support a credible natural experiment.
examples.zh: 我们讨论课堂时间表的变动能否支持一个可信的「自然实验」。

words.enDefinition: An assignment process treated as random for a comparison because it plausibly does not depend on relevant potential outcomes.

examples.en: The case assumes as-if random assignment for students placed in parallel sections by the timetable rule.
examples.zh: 案例假设时间表规则把学生分到平行班的过程属于「近似随机分配」。

examples.en: Group similarity alone did not persuade the class that as-if random assignment held in the example.
examples.zh: 两组相似这一点本身不足以让全班相信示例中的「近似随机分配」成立。

words.zhGloss: 基于可观测变量的选择
words.enDefinition: The assumption that after conditioning on observed characteristics, treatment assignment is independent of relevant potential outcomes.
acceptedZhAnswers: 基于可观测变量的选择

examples.en: Selection on observables assumes the measured characteristics account for systematic treatment selection in the example.
examples.zh: 在示例中，「基于可观测变量的选择」假设实测特征足以解释处理分配中的系统性选择。

examples.en: We discussed whether selection on observables was plausible given the limited information about prior achievement.
examples.zh: 鉴于掌握的既往成绩信息有限，我们讨论了「基于可观测变量的选择」是否可信。

words.enDefinition: The assumption that comparable covariate profiles have positive probabilities of being both treated and untreated.

examples.en: The overlap assumption fails in the example when every student with a certain score receives tutoring.
examples.zh: 示例中，当某一分数的学生全部接受辅导时，「重叠性假设」不成立。

examples.en: We examined the observed scores to assess whether the overlap assumption looked plausible in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们查看实测分数，评估「重叠性假设」是否可信。

words.enDefinition: The probability of treatment conditional on a set of observed characteristics.

examples.en: The propensity score uses observed grades and attendance to estimate tutoring participation in the example.
examples.zh: 示例中的「倾向得分」利用实测成绩和出勤率估计参加辅导的概率。

examples.en: We compared the estimated propensity score distributions of the two groups before making any outcome comparisons.
examples.zh: 在比较结果之前，我们先比较两组估计的「倾向得分」分布。

words.enDefinition: Similarity in the distributions of observed characteristics across the groups being compared.

examples.en: We checked covariate balance by comparing prior grades in the fictional treatment and comparison groups.
examples.zh: 我们通过比较虚构处理组与比较组的既往成绩，检查「协变量平衡」。

examples.en: The adjusted groups showed better covariate balance on attendance than they did before the adjustment.
examples.zh: 调整之后，各组在出勤率上的「协变量平衡」比调整前更好。

words.enDefinition: A situation in which the outcome for one unit depends on another unit's treatment assignment.

examples.en: Interference between units is possible when students in different groups share worked examples after the session.
examples.zh: 不同组的学生在课后分享解题示例时，可能出现「单位间干扰」。

examples.en: We considered interference between units before treating outcomes at the two nearby schools as unaffected by each other.
examples.zh: 把两所邻近学校的结果视为互不影响之前，我们先考虑了「单位间干扰」。

collocations: assumption of no interference between units

words.enDefinition: A variable used to isolate exogenous variation in an endogenous regressor under specified validity conditions.

examples.en: The class considered a simulated offer as an instrumental variable for actual participation in tutoring.
examples.zh: 全班考虑用模拟邀请作为实际参加辅导的「工具变量」。

examples.en: We listed the assumptions required before treating the lottery result as an instrumental variable.
examples.zh: 我们先列出了把抽签结果当作「工具变量」所需的假设。

words.enDefinition: The requirement that an instrument provides variation in the endogenous regressor it is used for.

examples.en: Instrument relevance requires that the simulated offer changes the likelihood of taking part in tutoring.
examples.zh: 「工具变量相关性」要求模拟邀请改变参加辅导的可能性。

examples.en: We discussed instrument relevance after comparing attendance rates across the two randomized offer groups.
examples.zh: 我们比较两个随机邀请组的出席率之后，讨论了「工具变量相关性」。

words.enDefinition: The requirement that an instrument is independent of, or uncorrelated with, relevant unobserved outcome determinants under the model.

examples.en: Our instrument exogeneity discussion asks whether the lottery result is related to unmeasured student abilities.
examples.zh: 关于「工具变量外生性」的讨论要求判断抽签结果是否与未测量的学生能力有关。

examples.en: We stated instrument exogeneity separately from the assumption about the instrument's link to participation.
examples.zh: 我们把「工具变量外生性」和工具变量与参与之间关联的假设分别写明。

words.enDefinition: The assumption that an instrument can affect the outcome only by changing the treatment or endogenous regressor.

examples.en: The exclusion restriction would fail if a training offer improved scores through advice given before enrolment.
examples.zh: 如果培训邀请附带的报名指导能提高成绩，「排除限制」就不成立。

examples.en: We explained why the exclusion restriction matters before interpreting the example's instrumental variable estimate.
examples.zh: 解读示例的工具变量估计之前，我们先解释了「排除限制」为何重要。

words.enDefinition: An instrument with too little predictive power for the endogenous regressor to support conventional inference reliably.

examples.en: The hypothetical weak instrument barely changes participation, making the resulting estimates unreliable in the exercise.
examples.zh: 假设的「弱工具变量」几乎不改变参与率，使练习中的估计结果不可靠。

examples.en: We compared the uncertainty from a weak instrument with that from a stronger candidate in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们比较「弱工具变量」与另一个更强候选变量带来的不确定性。

words.enDefinition: The regression of an endogenous regressor on the instruments and any included exogenous controls in two-stage least squares.

examples.en: The first-stage regression shows how the simulated offer predicts actual attendance after accounting for prior scores.
examples.zh: 「第一阶段回归」展示控制先前成绩后，模拟邀请如何预测实际出席。

examples.en: We examined the first-stage regression before interpreting the second regression in the classroom example.
examples.zh: 在解读课堂示例的第二个回归前，我们先检查「第一阶段回归」。

words.enDefinition: The change in the outcome associated with a change in the instrument before scaling by its first-stage effect.

examples.en: The reduced-form effect compares mean scores by the offer in the randomized classroom tutoring example.
examples.zh: 在课堂随机辅导示例中，「简约式效应」根据是否获得邀请比较平均成绩。

examples.en: We divided the reduced-form effect by the first-stage difference in the simple binary example.
examples.zh: 在简单二元示例中，我们将「简约式效应」除以第一阶段差异。

words.enDefinition: An instrumental variable estimator that first projects endogenous regressors on the instruments and controls, then uses the fitted values in the outcome equation.

examples.en: We used two-stage least squares to estimate the simulated tutoring effect under the stated instrument assumptions.
examples.zh: 我们在给定的工具变量假设下，用「两阶段最小二乘法」估计模拟辅导的效果。

examples.en: The tutor showed how two-stage least squares uses predicted participation in the outcome equation.
examples.zh: 老师演示了「两阶段最小二乘法」如何在结果方程中使用预测参与值。

words.enDefinition: The average causal effect for units whose treatment status changes with the instrument, under suitable identification assumptions.

examples.en: The local average treatment effect describes the students who participate only when offered tutoring in our example.
examples.zh: 示例中的「局部平均处理效应」针对只有获得邀请才会参加辅导的学生。

examples.en: We explained why the local average treatment effect need not describe every student in the simulation.
examples.zh: 我们解释了为什么「局部平均处理效应」未必适用于模拟中的每名学生。

collocations: identify a local average treatment effect
estimate a local average treatment effect
interpret a local average treatment effect

words.enDefinition: A unit that takes treatment when the instrument encourages it and does not take treatment otherwise.

examples.en: A complier in the classroom example attends tutoring only when assigned to receive an offer.
examples.zh: 课堂示例中的「依从者」只有被分到获邀组时才参加辅导。

examples.en: We described a complier using both possible participation decisions in the worksheet's hypothetical scenario.
examples.zh: 我们用练习假设情境中的两种可能参与决策来描述「依从者」。

words.enDefinition: for a binary instrument, the assumption that moving from one instrument value to the other can only change treatment in a common direction

examples.en: Instrument monotonicity rules out students who would attend only when they did not receive an offer.
examples.zh: 「工具变量单调性」排除了只有没收到邀请才参加的学生。

examples.en: We discussed instrument monotonicity when interpreting which group the estimated effect would describe in the simulation.
examples.zh: 解释估计效应适用于模拟中哪一组时，我们讨论了「工具变量单调性」。

words.enDefinition: Data that follow the same units, such as people or schools, over multiple periods.

examples.en: The panel data follow the same schools from two years before tutoring to two years afterward.
examples.zh: 这组「面板数据」跟踪同一批学校，从辅导开始前两年一直到开始后两年。

examples.en: We used panel data to compare each fictional student's attendance before and after a change.
examples.zh: 我们用「面板数据」比较每名虚构学生在某项变化前后的出勤情况。

words.enDefinition: A panel in which every unit has observations in the same set of periods.

examples.en: The classroom file is a balanced panel because every school appears in all four years.
examples.zh: 课堂文件是「平衡面板」，因为每所学校在四个年度都有记录。

examples.en: We constructed a balanced panel for the exercise by retaining schools with records in every period.
examples.zh: 我们保留各期都有记录的学校，为练习构建了「平衡面板」。

words.enDefinition: A panel in which the set of observed periods varies across units.

examples.en: The sample becomes an unbalanced panel when two schools have no measured outcomes in one year.
examples.zh: 当两所学校在某年没有实测结果时，样本就变成了「非平衡面板」。

examples.en: We read the notes on the unbalanced panel before comparing estimates across the two classroom exercises.
examples.zh: 比较两个课堂练习的估计前，我们先读了这份「非平衡面板」的说明。

words.enDefinition: A sampling design that draws separate cross-sectional samples over time without following the same units.

examples.en: The repeated cross-section surveys new workers each year instead of following the same people over time.
examples.zh: 「重复横截面」每年调查新的一批劳动者，没有持续跟踪同一批人。

examples.en: We used repeated cross-section data to compare average outcomes across the two districts over time.
examples.zh: 我们使用「重复横截面」数据，比较两个地区的平均结果随时间的变化。

words.enDefinition: Changes in a measured variable across observations for the same unit, often over time.

examples.en: The estimate uses within-unit variation in study hours rather than differences between students in the worksheet.
examples.zh: 练习里的估计利用学习时数的「单位内变动」，不使用学生之间的差异。

examples.en: The graph shows within-unit variation for each school over the four periods in the example.
examples.zh: 图表显示示例中各学校在四期中的「单位内变动」。

words.enDefinition: Differences in a measured variable across units such as workers, schools, or regions.

examples.en: Between-unit variation captures differences across the schools in the classroom average attendance table for one year.
examples.zh: 「单位间变动」反映课堂表格中同一年各学校平均出勤率的差异。

examples.en: The tutor separated between-unit variation from changes over time within each fictional school in the dataset.
examples.zh: 老师把「单位间变动」与数据集中各虚构学校内部随时间的变化区分开。

words.zhGloss: 不随时间变化的协变量
words.enDefinition: A measured characteristic that remains constant over time for a given unit.
acceptedZhAnswers: 不随时间变化的协变量

examples.en: The exercise treats a school's original building location as a time-invariant covariate in the sample.
examples.zh: 在样本中，练习把学校最初的建筑位置看作「不随时间变化的协变量」。

examples.en: We discussed why a time-invariant covariate cannot be identified separately from unit effects in this model.
examples.zh: 我们讨论为什么这个模型里的「不随时间变化的协变量」无法与单位效应分开识别。

words.enDefinition: A measured characteristic that can take different values for the same unit across periods.

examples.en: The school's average class size serves as a time-varying covariate in the classroom panel regression.
examples.zh: 课堂面板回归将学校平均班级规模作为「随时间变化的协变量」。

examples.en: We checked when the time-varying covariate was recorded relative to the tutoring offer in each school.
examples.zh: 我们核对了各校记录该「随时间变化的协变量」与发出辅导邀请的先后顺序。

words.enDefinition: Terms that allow each observed unit to have its own constant baseline in a panel regression.

examples.en: Unit fixed effects absorb stable differences between schools in the classroom example of changes in attendance.
examples.zh: 在课堂出勤变化示例里，「单位固定效应」吸收各学校之间不随时间变化的差异。

examples.en: We included unit fixed effects so the comparison used changes within each fictional school over time.
examples.zh: 我们加入「单位固定效应」，让比较利用各所虚构学校内部随时间的变化。

words.enDefinition: Terms that allow each time period to have its own baseline shared by all units.

examples.en: Time fixed effects account for changes common to all schools in each year of the exercise.
examples.zh: 「时间固定效应」考虑练习中每年在所有学校都出现的变化。

examples.en: We included time fixed effects to distinguish shared yearly movements from differences across the individual schools.
examples.zh: 我们加入「时间固定效应」，将各校共有的年度变动与学校间差异区分开。

words.enDefinition: A regression specification that includes fixed effects for both units and time periods.

examples.en: The two-way fixed effects model includes separate terms for each school and each year in the sample.
examples.zh: 「双向固定效应」模型分别为样本里的学校和年份设置独立项。

examples.en: We discussed when two-way fixed effects could mix different treatment effects across adoption cohorts in the exercise.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了练习中「双向固定效应」何时会把不同项目启动批次的处理效应混在一起。

words.enDefinition: A transformation that subtracts each unit's mean from its observed values to remove time-invariant unit effects.

examples.en: The within transformation subtracts each school's average from the corresponding observations in the classroom panel.
examples.zh: 「组内变换」从课堂面板中各学校的观测值减去该校平均值。

examples.en: We applied the within transformation before fitting the unit fixed effects model on the worksheet.
examples.zh: 在练习纸上拟合单位固定效应模型前，我们先做了「组内变换」。

words.enDefinition: An estimator that removes or accounts for group-specific constant effects in a regression, such as unit effects.

examples.en: The fixed effects estimator uses the changes within each school to estimate the association in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，「固定效应估计量」利用各校内部的变化估计关联。

examples.en: We compared the fixed effects estimator with one that uses both within and between variation.
examples.zh: 我们比较了「固定效应估计量」与同时利用组内和组间变动的估计量。

words.enDefinition: A panel model that treats unit-specific effects as random components, conventionally assumed unrelated to the regressors.

examples.en: The random effects model assumes the school component is unrelated to the explanatory variables in this exercise.
examples.zh: 这项练习的「随机效应模型」假定学校效应分量与各解释变量无关。

examples.en: We discussed the assumptions behind the random effects model before comparing it with fixed effects.
examples.zh: 将「随机效应模型」与固定效应模型比较之前，我们先讨论其背后的假设。

collocations: assumptions of a random effects model

words.enDefinition: Dependence between a unit's disturbances across periods in a model with a time dimension.

examples.en: Serial correlation in errors occurs when a school's unmeasured attendance shocks persist across years in the exercise.
examples.zh: 练习中，一所学校未测量的出勤冲击跨年持续时，就存在「误差的序列相关」。

examples.en: The tutor discussed serial correlation in errors before explaining why the original uncertainty estimates might be too small.
examples.zh: 老师先讲「误差的序列相关」，再解释原来的不确定性估计为何可能过小。

collocations: allow for serial correlation in errors
serial correlation in errors over time

words.enDefinition: A measure of coefficient uncertainty that allows disturbances to be dependent within specified clusters under appropriate conditions.

examples.en: We reported a cluster-robust standard error that allowed observations within the same school to be related.
examples.zh: 我们报告了「聚类稳健标准误」，允许同一学校内的观测之间有关联。

examples.en: The cluster-robust standard error changed when the class grouped classroom observations by school instead of student.
examples.zh: 全班改按学校给课堂观测分组时，「聚类稳健标准误」发生了变化。

words.enDefinition: The unit of grouping used to allow for dependence when calculating clustered uncertainty estimates.

examples.en: We chose a school clustering level because the hypothetical offer was assigned to schools as groups.
examples.zh: 假设邀请以学校为单位分配，因此我们选择学校作为「聚类层级」。

examples.en: The report states the clustering level below the estimates so readers can interpret the uncertainty.
examples.zh: 报告在估计值下方说明「聚类层级」，方便读者解读不确定性。

words.enDefinition: Statistical inference in settings with too few independent clusters for usual large-cluster approximations to be reliable.

examples.en: Few-cluster inference matters in the exercise because only six fictional schools could receive the offer.
examples.zh: 练习里只有六所虚构学校有机会收到邀请，所以「少聚类推断」很重要。

examples.en: The tutor covered few-cluster inference to explain why many students cannot replace many independent schools here.
examples.zh: 老师用「少聚类推断」解释为什么在这里，增加学生人数无法替代增加独立学校的数量。

words.enDefinition: A method that compares changes over time in a treated group with changes in a comparison group.

examples.en: Difference-in-differences compares the change in attendance at treated schools with the change at comparison schools.
examples.zh: 「双重差分法」把接受处理的学校与比较学校的出勤率变化进行比较。

examples.en: We used difference-in-differences under stated assumptions to estimate the effect of the simulated tutoring programme.
examples.zh: 我们在给定假设下，使用「双重差分法」估计模拟辅导项目的效应。

words.enDefinition: the assumption that the compared groups' average outcomes would have changed by the same amount over the relevant periods without treatment

examples.en: The parallel trends assumption concerns the changes that would have occurred without tutoring in our example.
examples.zh: 示例中的「平行趋势假设」针对的是没有辅导时本会发生的变化。

examples.en: We stated the parallel trends assumption before showing the curves for the two fictional groups.
examples.zh: 我们先说明「平行趋势假设」，再展示两个虚构组的曲线。

collocations: violation of the parallel trends assumption

words.enDefinition: The pattern of outcome changes in periods before a unit or group receives treatment.

examples.en: The pre-treatment trend in attendance looks similar across the two schools in the classroom graph.
examples.zh: 课堂图中，两所学校出勤率的「处理前趋势」看起来相近。

examples.en: We looked at the pre-treatment trend before interpreting the large difference that appeared after tutoring.
examples.zh: 我们先查看「处理前趋势」，再解读辅导实施后出现的较大差异。

words.enDefinition: The assumption that future treatment does not affect outcomes before the designated start of treatment.

examples.en: The no anticipation assumption would fail if students changed attendance before the scheduled start of tutoring.
examples.zh: 如果学生在辅导计划开始前就改变出勤情况，「无预期效应假设」就不成立。

examples.en: Our study design states the no anticipation assumption next to the programme's announced start date.
examples.zh: 我们的研究设计在项目宣布的开始日期旁写明「无预期效应假设」。

collocations: violation of the no anticipation assumption

words.enDefinition: The introduction of treatment at different times for different units or groups in the same study.

examples.en: Staggered adoption occurs because the fictional schools start tutoring in three different years in the example.
examples.zh: 示例中的虚构学校在三个不同年度启动辅导，因此属于「分期实施」。

examples.en: We drew a timeline to show how staggered adoption affects who remains available for comparison.
examples.zh: 我们画了一条时间线，说明「分期实施」会如何影响仍可用作比较的学校。

words.enDefinition: A group of units that first receive treatment in the same period in a staggered design.

examples.en: The first treatment cohort contains the fictional schools that began tutoring in the first year.
examples.zh: 第一个「处理批次」包含第一年开始辅导的虚构学校。

examples.en: We estimated a separate effect for each treatment cohort before combining them in our example.
examples.zh: 在示例中，我们先为各「处理批次」分别估计效应，再将它们合并。

words.enDefinition: Units that do not receive treatment during the observed period and serve as a comparison group.

examples.en: The never-treated comparison group contains schools without a tutoring programme during the entire classroom study.
examples.zh: 「始终未处理比较组」由课堂研究期间一直没有辅导项目的学校组成。

examples.en: We used the never-treated comparison group as a reference when estimating effects for the earliest cohort.
examples.zh: 估计最早批次的效应时，我们参考了「始终未处理比较组」。

words.enDefinition: Units used as comparisons before their own treatment starts, although they may receive treatment later.

examples.en: The not-yet-treated comparison group includes schools due to start tutoring next year in the exercise.
examples.zh: 练习里的「尚未处理比较组」包括预计明年启动辅导的学校。

examples.en: We updated the not-yet-treated comparison group once another set of fictional schools began the tutoring programme.
examples.zh: 另一批虚构学校开始辅导项目后，我们更新了「尚未处理比较组」。

words.enDefinition: A model indexed by time relative to treatment that can estimate effects by period under stated assumptions.

examples.en: The event study specification allows the fitted attendance effects to differ across relative years in our example.
examples.zh: 示例中的「事件研究设定」允许拟合的出勤效应随相对年份而变化。

examples.en: We wrote an event study specification with indicators for the periods before and after tutoring.
examples.zh: 我们写出一套「事件研究设定」，加入辅导前后各期的指示变量。

words.enDefinition: Time measured relative to when a unit first experiences an event or begins treatment.

examples.en: Event time equals zero in the year when each fictional school first begins offering tutoring.
examples.zh: 各所虚构学校第一次开始辅导的那一年，「事件相对时间」等于零。

examples.en: We aligned the outcome series by event time so that the different starting years could be compared.
examples.zh: 我们按「事件相对时间」对齐结果序列，以便比较不同起始年份。

words.enDefinition: A regression coefficient associated with a particular period relative to treatment in an event study.

examples.en: The event-time coefficient for the first year after tutoring is positive in the simulated exercise.
examples.zh: 在模拟练习里，开始辅导后第一年的「事件相对时间系数」为正。

examples.en: We plotted each event-time coefficient with an interval to show the uncertainty around the estimate.
examples.zh: 我们为每个「事件相对时间系数」画出区间，展示估计的不确定性。

words.enDefinition: The relative period left out of an event study so coefficients refer to changes from that period.

examples.en: The omitted event period is the year immediately before tutoring starts in this classroom example.
examples.zh: 课堂示例中，「省略的事件参照期」是辅导启动前一年。

examples.en: We named the omitted event period in the chart caption to make the comparison clear.
examples.zh: 我们在图注里注明「省略的事件参照期」，使比较基准更清楚。

words.enDefinition: A check for systematic differences in group trends before treatment, which may reveal concerns about identification.

examples.en: The pre-trend test checks whether estimated differences were already changing before the hypothetical programme began.
examples.zh: 「处理前趋势检验」查看在假设项目开始前，估计差异是否已经在变化。

examples.en: The tutor explained why passing a pre-trend test cannot establish the required counterfactual trend assumption.
examples.zh: 老师解释了为什么通过「处理前趋势检验」无法证实所需的反事实趋势假设。

words.zhGloss: 组别—时间平均处理效应
words.enDefinition: The average treatment effect for a specified treatment cohort in a particular calendar period.
acceptedZhAnswers: 组别—时间平均处理效应

examples.en: The group-time average treatment effect describes one cohort's outcomes in one year of the example.
examples.zh: 「组别—时间平均处理效应」描述示例中某个处理批次在指定一年的结果效应。

examples.en: We computed a group-time average treatment effect before combining estimates across the fictional school cohorts.
examples.zh: 我们先计算「组别—时间平均处理效应」，再合并不同虚构学校批次的估计。

collocations: estimate a group-time average treatment effect
display a group-time average treatment effect

words.enDefinition: An underlying time trend allowed to vary by group in a model.

examples.en: The sensitivity exercise adds a group-specific trend to allow the two districts to evolve differently.
examples.zh: 敏感性练习加入「组别特定趋势」，让两个地区可有不同的发展趋势。

examples.en: We explained the extra assumptions needed when including a group-specific trend in this classroom model.
examples.zh: 我们解释了在课堂模型中加入「组别特定趋势」所需的额外假设。

words.enDefinition: A design that uses a cutoff in treatment assignment to estimate an effect near the cutoff under stated assumptions.

examples.en: The regression discontinuity design compares students with scores just above and below the fictional eligibility cutoff.
examples.zh: 「断点回归设计」比较得分刚超过和刚低于虚构资格门槛的学生。

examples.en: We stated the assignment rule before explaining why the regression discontinuity design was plausible here.
examples.zh: 我们先说明分配规则，再解释「断点回归设计」在这个案例里为何可信。

collocations: assumptions of a regression discontinuity design
estimate with a regression discontinuity design

words.enDefinition: A score or measured quantity whose position relative to a threshold governs treatment assignment or its probability.

examples.en: The running variable is the initial test score used to decide eligibility for simulated tutoring.
examples.zh: 「驱动变量」是决定学生有无模拟辅导资格的初始测试成绩。

examples.en: We plotted the running variable on the horizontal axis of the classroom discontinuity graph.
examples.zh: 我们把「驱动变量」画在课堂断点图的横轴上。

words.enDefinition: The threshold of the running variable at which treatment status or its probability changes.

examples.en: The assignment cutoff in the exercise is the score that changes access to extra classes.
examples.zh: 练习中的「分配阈值」是能改变学生获取额外课程机会的分数。

examples.en: We marked the assignment cutoff with a vertical line on the graph of simulated scores.
examples.zh: 我们在模拟成绩图上用竖线标出「分配阈值」。

words.enDefinition: A discontinuity design in which treatment status changes deterministically across the assignment cutoff.

examples.en: Sharp regression discontinuity applies in the example because every eligible student receives tutoring and nobody else does.
examples.zh: 示例适合「精确断点回归」，因为每名符合资格的学生都接受辅导，其余学生均不参加。

examples.en: We started with sharp regression discontinuity before studying a less strictly enforced eligibility rule in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们先学习「精确断点回归」，再看执行较灵活的资格规则。

words.enDefinition: A discontinuity design in which the cutoff changes treatment probability without perfectly determining each unit's treatment status.

examples.en: Fuzzy regression discontinuity fits the example because the cutoff changes participation without fully determining it.
examples.zh: 「模糊断点回归」适用于该示例，因为跨过阈值会改变参加概率，但无法完全决定是否参加。

examples.en: The tutor used fuzzy regression discontinuity to distinguish eligibility from actual participation in the simulation.
examples.zh: 老师用「模糊断点回归」区分模拟中的资格与实际参与。

collocations: participation jump in fuzzy regression discontinuity

words.enDefinition: In a regression discontinuity design, the assumption that the conditional mean of each potential outcome is continuous at the cutoff.

examples.en: The continuity assumption would be doubtful if another service also changed abruptly at the same cutoff.
examples.zh: 如果另一项服务也在同一阈值处突然变化，「连续性假设」就值得怀疑。

examples.en: We stated the continuity assumption before interpreting the apparent jump in the classroom outcome graph.
examples.zh: 我们先明确「连续性假设」，再解读课堂结果图上看似突然的跳变。

words.enDefinition: A straight-line model estimated using observations near a chosen target value, often with distance-based weights.

examples.en: The local linear fit uses scores close to the cutoff in the simulated tutoring data.
examples.zh: 「局部线性拟合」使用模拟辅导数据中接近阈值的成绩。

examples.en: We estimated a local linear fit on each side to compare their values at the cutoff.
examples.zh: 我们在阈值两侧分别进行「局部线性拟合」，以比较两侧在阈值处的数值。

words.enDefinition: A distance scale around the cutoff used to choose or weight observations for a discontinuity estimate.

examples.en: The RD bandwidth determines how far from the cutoff observations contribute to the local estimate.
examples.zh: 「断点回归带宽」决定距阈值多远的观测会用于局部估计。

examples.en: We used a smaller RD bandwidth to focus the classroom exercise on scores near eligibility.
examples.zh: 我们使用较小的「断点回归带宽」，让课堂练习聚焦资格阈值附近的成绩。

words.enDefinition: The extent to which a local estimate changes when the bandwidth is changed.

examples.en: We checked bandwidth sensitivity by comparing estimates that use scores at different distances from the cutoff.
examples.zh: 我们比较使用距阈值不同距离的成绩得到的估计，以检查「带宽敏感性」。

examples.en: The report describes bandwidth sensitivity because the estimated jump changes across reasonable choices in the exercise.
examples.zh: 练习中，不同合理带宽下的估计跳变有所变化，报告因此说明「带宽敏感性」。

words.zhGloss: 阈值附近的选择性分布
words.enDefinition: Nonrandom placement of units on either side of a cutoff, for example through influence over the running variable.
acceptedZhAnswers: 阈值附近的选择性分布

examples.en: The class discussed whether sorting around the cutoff could make the two groups systematically different.
examples.zh: 全班讨论「阈值附近的选择性分布」会不会让两组存在系统差异。

examples.en: The worksheet asks what patterns might suggest sorting around the cutoff in the simulated records.
examples.zh: 练习要求判断模拟记录中的哪些模式可能提示「阈值附近的选择性分布」。

collocations: signs of sorting around the cutoff

words.enDefinition: A diagnostic for a jump in the distribution density of the running variable at the cutoff.

examples.en: The density continuity test checks whether example scores cluster unevenly just above and below the cutoff.
examples.zh: 「密度连续性检验」检查示例成绩在阈值上下一小段范围内的集中程度是否不均。

examples.en: We interpreted the density continuity test alongside the known rules for assigning scores in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们结合已知的评分规则解读「密度连续性检验」。

collocations: density continuity test at the cutoff

words.enDefinition: A sensitivity design that re-estimates a discontinuity after excluding observations nearest to the assignment cutoff.

examples.en: Donut regression discontinuity excludes the scores nearest the threshold in our simulated classroom study.
examples.zh: 在模拟课堂研究里，「环形断点回归」排除最靠近阈值的成绩。

examples.en: We compared donut regression discontinuity results with estimates using all scores near the fictional threshold.
examples.zh: 我们把「环形断点回归」结果与使用虚构阈值附近全部成绩的估计作了比较。

words.enDefinition: An artificial cutoff with no known treatment change, used to check for unexplained discontinuities.

examples.en: The placebo cutoff is set at a score where no eligibility rule changes in the exercise.
examples.zh: 练习中的「安慰剂阈值」设在资格规则没有发生变化的分数处。

examples.en: We explained why a jump at a placebo cutoff would complicate interpreting the main result.
examples.zh: 我们解释为什么在「安慰剂阈值」处出现跳变会让主要结果更难解释。

words.enDefinition: Continuity of the conditional means of pre-treatment characteristics across the cutoff, used as a design check.

examples.en: We checked covariate continuity by looking for a jump in prior grades at the threshold.
examples.zh: 我们查看阈值处既往成绩是否跳变，以检查「协变量连续性」。

examples.en: The tutor explained how a failure of covariate continuity could weaken confidence in the design.
examples.zh: 老师解释「协变量连续性」不成立为何会削弱对设计的信心。

words.enDefinition: the treatment effect identified at the assignment cutoff under the assumptions of the particular regression discontinuity design

examples.en: The local effect at the cutoff concerns students near eligibility in the simulated tutoring example.
examples.zh: 在模拟辅导示例中，「阈值处局部效应」针对接近资格门槛的学生。

examples.en: We discussed why the local effect at the cutoff need not apply to students far away.
examples.zh: 我们讨论「阈值处局部效应」为什么未必适用于得分离阈值很远的学生。

collocations: estimate a local effect at the cutoff
interpret the local effect at the cutoff
report a local effect at the cutoff

words.enDefinition: The effect of being assigned or offered treatment, regardless of whether a unit actually receives it.

examples.en: The intent-to-treat effect compares students by their assigned offer rather than by attendance in the simulation.
examples.zh: 这次模拟里的「意向处理效应」按学生是否被分配到获邀组比较，不按实际出席划分。

examples.en: We estimated the intent-to-treat effect even though some students did not attend the offered tutoring.
examples.zh: 尽管有些获邀学生没有参加辅导，我们仍估计了「意向处理效应」。

words.enDefinition: A situation in which some units do not follow their assigned treatment status.

examples.en: Imperfect compliance occurs when some students assigned an offer choose not to attend the simulated tutoring.
examples.zh: 在模拟里，有些获邀学生选择不参加辅导，就出现了「不完全依从」。

examples.en: The exercise asks how imperfect compliance changes the interpretation of the effect of an offer.
examples.zh: 练习问「不完全依从」如何改变对邀请效应的解读。

words.enDefinition: The observations actually included in an estimate after applying the stated inclusion and exclusion rules.

examples.en: The analysis sample excludes schools that lack a usable outcome for the chosen follow-up period.
examples.zh: 「分析样本」排除在选定随访期内没有可用结果的学校。

examples.en: We reported the size of the analysis sample for each column in the classroom results table.
examples.zh: 我们在课堂结果表的各列报告对应「分析样本」的规模。

words.enDefinition: Bias that arises when inclusion in the analysed sample depends on factors related to the outcome or its determinants.

examples.en: Sample selection bias may arise when wages are observed only for employed participants in the example.
examples.zh: 示例只观测到在职参与者的工资，这可能产生「样本选择偏误」。

examples.en: We considered sample selection bias before interpreting results from the smaller group with recorded outcomes.
examples.zh: 我们先考虑「样本选择偏误」，再解读有记录结果的较小组得出的结果。

words.enDefinition: A difference in the rate or pattern of loss to follow-up across groups being compared.

examples.en: Differential attrition could occur if a smaller share of one group completes the final classroom survey.
examples.zh: 如果课堂调查中一个组完成末次问卷的学生比例较低，就可能出现「差异性流失」。

examples.en: We checked differential attrition before interpreting the final comparison between the two fictional study groups.
examples.zh: 我们先查「差异性流失」，再解读两个虚构研究组之间的最终比较。

words.enDefinition: Additive measurement noise that is unrelated to the true value, with further independence conditions specified by the model.

examples.en: The simulation adds classical measurement error to true study hours without following any systematic pattern.
examples.zh: 模拟给真实学习时数加入「经典测量误差」，误差不遵循任何系统模式。

examples.en: We contrasted classical measurement error with a case where larger true values lead to larger errors.
examples.zh: 我们把「经典测量误差」与真值越大、误差也越大的情况作了比较。

collocations: classical measurement error in a regressor

words.enDefinition: A bias toward zero, as occurs for the slope in simple regression with classical regressor measurement error.

examples.en: Attenuation bias pulls the slope toward zero when the only regressor contains classical measurement error.
examples.zh: 唯一的解释变量带有经典测量误差时，「衰减偏误」会让斜率趋向零。

examples.en: The simulated comparison makes attenuation bias visible by contrasting slopes from true and noisy study hours.
examples.zh: 模拟用真实和带噪声的学习时数拟合斜率，比较后能看出「衰减偏误」。

words.enDefinition: An analysis that tests whether a substantive conclusion persists under a reasonable change in the method or data.

examples.en: The robustness check uses a different comparison school to see whether the main pattern persists.
examples.zh: 「稳健性检查」使用另一所比较学校，看看主要模式是否仍然存在。

examples.en: We described each robustness check alongside the assumptions it changes in the classroom report.
examples.zh: 我们在课堂报告说明每项「稳健性检查」以及它改变的假设。

words.enDefinition: A different credible model setup used to compare how estimates depend on model choices.

examples.en: The alternative specification includes a separate time trend for each district in our practice table.
examples.zh: 练习表里的「替代设定」为每个地区加入单独的时间趋势。

examples.en: We compared the baseline result with an alternative specification that used fewer control variables.
examples.zh: 我们把基准结果与采用较少控制变量的「替代设定」作了比较。

words.enDefinition: A diagnostic that tests for an effect in a deliberately chosen situation where the treatment should have none.

examples.en: The placebo test pretends tutoring started a year earlier to check for an apparent premature effect.
examples.zh: 「安慰剂检验」假定辅导提前一年开始，以检查是否会估计出过早出现的效应。

examples.en: An unexpected estimate in the placebo test led us to revisit the assignment assumptions in class.
examples.zh: 课堂「安慰剂检验」出现意外估计值后，我们重新检查了分配假设。

words.enDefinition: An outcome used in a diagnostic because it should not be causally affected by the treatment.

examples.en: The study uses scores recorded before tutoring as a placebo outcome in the classroom exercise.
examples.zh: 课堂练习用辅导前记录的成绩作为「安慰剂结果变量」。

examples.en: We explained why an estimated effect on the placebo outcome would raise doubts about comparability.
examples.zh: 我们解释，为什么估计发现处理影响「安慰剂结果变量」会让人怀疑各组是否可比。

words.enDefinition: A sensitivity check that re-estimates a result after removing each cluster in turn.

examples.en: Our leave-one-cluster-out check asks whether the estimated attendance change depends heavily on one fictional school.
examples.zh: 我们的「逐簇剔除检查」考察出勤率的估计变化是否高度依赖某一所虚构学校。

examples.en: We plotted the leave-one-cluster-out check results after repeating the analysis without each school in turn.
examples.zh: 我们依次剔除每所学校、重做分析，然后绘出「逐簇剔除检查」结果。

words.enDefinition: An observation whose removal or alteration substantially changes the fitted model or an estimate of interest.

examples.en: One influential observation changes the fitted wage relationship substantially when removed from the classroom dataset.
examples.zh: 从课堂数据集中移除某个「高影响观测值」，拟合的工资关系就会明显变化。

examples.en: We investigated the influential observation to check the recorded units before repeating the regression.
examples.zh: 我们检查这个「高影响观测值」的记录单位，再重新做回归。

words.enDefinition: The extent to which an estimated coefficient remains similar across reasonable model choices or samples.

examples.en: The coefficient stability exercise compares estimates after adding two sets of controls to the wage regression.
examples.zh: 「系数稳定性」练习比较工资回归分别加入两组控制变量之后的估计。

examples.en: We assessed coefficient stability by fitting the same model in two related classroom samples.
examples.zh: 我们用两个相关的课堂样本拟合同一模型，以评估「系数稳定性」。

words.enDefinition: the difference between an estimator's expected value at the given finite sample size and the parameter it is estimating

examples.en: The simulation reveals finite-sample bias by averaging the estimates over many draws of ten observations.
examples.zh: 模拟对许多各含十个观测值的样本所得估计取平均，从而显示「有限样本偏误」。

examples.en: We discussed why finite-sample bias can be present even for an estimator that is consistent.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了为什么估计量即使具有一致性，也可能存在「有限样本偏误」。

words.enDefinition: Inference that uses a specified assignment or sampling design as the source of uncertainty about an estimate.

examples.en: Design-based inference uses the known lottery assignment to quantify uncertainty in the simulated tutoring result.
examples.zh: 「基于设计的推断」利用已知的抽签分配机制量化模拟辅导结果的不确定性。

examples.en: The lesson explains how design-based inference reflects which groups actually entered the classroom lottery.
examples.zh: 课上说明「基于设计的推断」如何反映哪些组实际参加了课堂抽签。

words.enDefinition: An effect large enough to matter in the economic context being studied.

examples.en: The seminar asks whether the small estimated wage difference represents an economically meaningful effect in this example.
examples.zh: 研讨课要求判断，示例中估计出的微小工资差异是否属于「具有经济意义的效应」。

examples.en: We judged whether the estimate represented an economically meaningful effect by comparing it with typical hourly pay.
examples.zh: 我们把估计值与典型小时工资比较，判断它是否代表「具有经济意义的效应」。

collocations: magnitude of an economically meaningful effect
